children.text: paraṃ parasthaṃ gahanād anādim ekaṃ niviṣṭaṃ bahudhā guhāsu |
children.translated_text: The Supreme, dwelling beyond, unfathomable, beginningless, one, yet entered into the many caves [of the heart],

children.text: sarvālayaṃ sarvacarācarasthaṃ tvām eva śambhuṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye || 1 ||
children.translated_text: the abode of all, residing in all that moves and is still—to You alone, O <s>Śambhu</s>, I take refuge. (1)
Bewildered by the wheel of suffering that begins with dwelling in the womb and ends with death,
the disciple asked the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), who is the foundation, about the highest truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). (2)

children.text: ādhārakārikābhiḥ taṃ gurur abhibhāṣati sma tatsāram |
children.translated_text: The teacher addressed him through the verses of the <s>Ādhārakārikā</s>, and its essence
<s>Abhinavagupta</s> expounds by means of the vision of <s>Śiva</s>'s teaching. (3)
From the fullness of the splendor of His own power (<s>śakti</s>), this fourfold egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>), in its divisions—

children.text: śaktir māyā prakṛtiḥ pṛthvī ceti prabhāvitaṃ prabhuṇā || 4 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Pṛthvī</s> (earth)—has been manifested by the Lord (<s>Prabhu</s>). (4)
Within that [fourfold egg] exists this entire universe, a continuous stream of diverse bodies, organs, and worlds,

children.text: bhoktā ca tatra dehī śiva eva gṛhītapaśubhāvaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and the experiencer therein, the embodied one, is none other than <s>Śiva</s> himself, having assumed the condition of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>). (5)
Just as a pure crystal takes on the appearance of colors of various kinds,
so too does the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) [take on] the forms of gods, humans, animals, and beings of the lower worlds. (6)

children.text: gacchati gacchati jala iva himakarabimbaṃ sthite sthitiṃ yāti |
children.translated_text: Just as the orb of the moon moves when the water moves, and stands still when it is still,
so does this Self (<s>Ātmā</s>), the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>), [appear to change] in the category of bodies, organs, and worlds. (7)

children.text: rāhur adṛśyo 'pi yathā śaśibimbasthaḥ prakāśate tadvat |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rāhu</s>, though invisible, becomes manifest when situated in the orb of the moon, so too
this Self (<s>Ātmā</s>), though all-pervading, [becomes manifest] in the mirror of cognition (<s>dhī</s>) through dependence on sense objects. (8)

children.text: ādarśe malarahite yadvad vadanaṃ vibhāti tadvad ayam |
children.translated_text: Just as the face shines in a mirror free of impurity, so does this [Self],
whose nature is luminosity (<s>bhārūpa</s>), shine in the principle of cognition (<s>dhītattva</s>) purified by the descent of <s>Śiva</s>'s grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>). (9)
Luminous in nature (<s>bhārūpa</s>), complete, of great bliss (<s>mahānanda</s>) through repose in one's own Self,
overflowing with will (<s>icchā</s>), consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), and activity (<s>karaṇa</s>), full of infinite powers (<s>śakti</s>). (10)
Devoid of all conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), pure, tranquil, free from dissolution and arising—

children.text: yat paratattvaṃ tasmin vibhāti ṣaṭṭriṃśadātma jagat || 11 ||
children.translated_text: in that supreme reality (<s>paratattva</s>), the universe of thirty-six [principles] shines. (11)
Just as in the image in a mirror, the variegated [picture] of a city, village, and the like appears undivided,

children.text: bhāti vibhāgenaiva ca parasparaṃ darpaṇād api ca || 12 ||
children.translated_text: yet shines as if divided from one another and also from the mirror— (12)
so too, from the most pure consciousness of the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, this universe, though devoid of division,

children.text: anyonyaṃ ca tato 'pi ca vibhaktam ābhāti jagad etat || 13 ||
children.translated_text: shines as if divided from one another and also from that [consciousness]. (13)
The tenfold [range of] principles—<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s>—
He causes to shine in the mode of division through the five <s>Śaktis</s>. (14)
That which is the supreme sovereignty of the great Lord (<s>Maheśa</s>), the accomplishment of the impossible—
that is the goddess <s>Māyāśakti</s>, the self-concealment of <s>Śiva</s>. (15)

children.text: māyāparigrahavaśād bodho malinaḥ pumān paśur bhavati |
children.translated_text: Due to the embrace of <s>Māyā</s>, consciousness becomes impure; the soul (<s>pumān</s>) becomes a bound being (<s>paśu</s>),
bound by the force of <s>Kāla</s> (time), <s>Kalā</s> (limited agency), <s>Niyati</s> (destiny), and <s>Bala</s> (limitation), and through <s>Rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance). (16)

children.text: adhunaiva kiṃcid evedam eva sarvātmanaiva jānāmi |
children.translated_text: "Only now, only something, only this, with my whole being I know"—

children.text: māyāsahitaṃ kañcukaṣaṭkam aṇor antaraṅgam idam uktam || 17 ||
children.translated_text: this sixfold covering (<s>kañcuka</s>), together with <s>Māyā</s>, is said to be the innermost [sheath] of the limited self (<s>aṇu</s>). (17)

children.text: kambukam iva ta.ṅdulakaṇaviniviṣṭaṃ bhinnam apy abhidā |
children.translated_text: Like the husk encasing a grain of rice, [the covering] though separate is undivided [from the soul],
but it attains purity through the practice of turning toward the path of <s>Śiva</s>. (18)
Pleasure, pain, and delusion alone [comprise <s>Prakṛti</s>]; and from determination, conceptualization, and self-attribution,
<s>Prakṛti</s> [gives rise to] the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>), in the order of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>manas</s> (mind), and <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego). (19)
Ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose are the cognitive sense organs (<s>buddhīndriyāṇi</s>), [operating] in the domain of sound and the rest;
speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are the organs of action (<s>karmendriyāṇi</s>). (20)

children.text: eṣāṃ grāhyo viṣayaḥ sūkṣmaḥ pravibhāgavarjito yaḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: The subtle object grasped by these, which is devoid of differentiation,

children.text: tanmātrapañcakaṃ tat śabdaḥ sparśo maho raso gandhaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: is the fivefold group of <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements): sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. (21)
From the combination of these [<s>tanmātras</s>], the gross objects assume the nature of the five elements (<s>bhūtapañcaka</s>):

children.text: abhyeti nabhaḥ pavanas tejaḥ salilaṃ ca pṛthvī ca || 22 ||
children.translated_text: space (<s>nabhas</s>), wind (<s>pavana</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), water (<s>salila</s>), and earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>). (22)

children.text: tuṣa iva ta.ṅdulakaṇikām āvṛṇute prakṛtipūrvakaḥ sargaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the husk encloses the grain of rice, so this creation beginning with <s>Prakṛti</s>
and extending down to earth envelops consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) in the form of a body. (23)

children.text: param āvaraṇaṃ mala iha sūkṣmaṃ māyādikañcukaṃ sthūlam |
children.translated_text: The supreme covering is <s>mala</s> (primal impurity)—here it is subtle; <s>Māyā</s> and its coverings (<s>kañcuka</s>) are gross;
the external [covering] is the body—thus the Self (<s>Ātmā</s>) is enveloped in three sheaths (<s>kośatraya</s>). (24)

children.text: ajñānatimirayogād ekam api svaṃ svabhāvam ātmānam |
children.translated_text: Due to conjunction with the darkness of ignorance, the Self (<s>Ātmā</s>), though one and of its own nature,
is apprehended in the diversity of manifold [forms as] grasped and grasper. (25)
Just as juice, raw sugar, refined sugar, molite, and candy are all [forms] of sugarcane juice alone,

children.text: tadvad avasthā bhedāḥ sarve paramātmanaḥ śambhoḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: so all the different states are [modifications] of the supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), <s>Śambhu</s>. (26)
<s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>antaryāmin</s> (inner controller), <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>virāj</s> (cosmic form), ending in body, species, and individual—

children.text: vyavahāramātram etat paramārthena tu na santy eva || 27 ||
children.translated_text: all this is merely conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>); in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) they do not exist at all. (27)

children.text: rajjvāṃ nāsti bhujaṅgas trāsaṃ kurute ca mṛtyuparyantam |
children.translated_text: The snake does not exist in the rope, yet it causes fear even unto death;

children.text: bhrānter mahatī śaktir na vivektuṃ śakyate nāma || 28 ||
children.translated_text: the power of delusion is indeed great—it truly cannot be analyzed. (28)
Likewise, <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), heaven and hell, birth and death, pleasure and pain—

children.text: varṇāśramādi cātmany asad api vibhramabalād bhavati || 29 ||
children.translated_text: though non-existent in the Self (<s>Ātman</s>), they arise through the force of delusion, along with <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life) and the rest. (29)

children.text: etat tad andhakāraṃ yad bhāveṣu prakāśamānatayā |
children.translated_text: This is that darkness: that in things which are appearances of consciousness,
even in what is not different from the Self, there arises this false identification with the not-self (<s>anātmābhimāna</s>). (30)

children.text: timirād api timiram idaṃ ga.ṅdasyopari mahān ayaṃ sphoṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is a darkness even beyond darkness, a great boil upon the [existing] boil:
that even in the not-self—the body, vital breath, and the like—there is the false identification with the Self. (31)
Through conjunction with the manifold of body, vital breath, reflection, cognition, knowledge, and space,

children.text: ātmānam veṣṭayate citraṃ jālena jālakāra iva || 32 ||
children.translated_text: the Self (<s>Ātmā</s>) envelops himself—wonderfully, like a spider with its own web. (32)
Through the practice of manifesting the splendor of self-knowledge, one should uncover one's own Self;
thus the supreme <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Paramaśiva</s>) unfolds the wondrous play of bondage and liberation. (33)
Creation, preservation, and dissolution; waking and dreaming; and deep sleep—these shine

children.text: bhānti turīye dhāmani tathāpi tair nāvṛtaṃ bhāti || 34 ||
children.translated_text: in that abode which is the fourth (<s>turīya</s>), yet it shines uncovered by them. (34)

children.text: jāgrad viśvaṃ bhedāt svapnas tejaḥ prakāśamāhātmyāt |
children.translated_text: The waking state is <s>Viśva</s> (the universal), due to [perception of] difference; the dream state is <s>Tejas</s> (luminous), due to the greatness of [inner] illumination;

children.text: prājñaḥ suptāvasthā jñānaghanatvāt tataḥ paraṃ turyam || 35 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> (the knower) is the state of deep sleep, due to being a mass of knowledge; beyond that is the fourth (<s>Turya</s>). (35)
Just as the vault of the sky is not made impure by clouds, smoke, and dust,
so the supreme Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>) is untouched by the modifications of <s>Māyā</s>. (36)

children.text: ekasmin ghaṭagagane rajasā vyāpte bhavanti nānyāni |
children.translated_text: When the space in one pot is pervaded by dust, the other [spaces in other pots] do not
become impure—likewise these individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>), who partake of the distinctions of pleasure and pain. (37)

children.text: śānte śānta ivāyaṃ hṛṣṭe hṛṣṭo vimohavati mūḍhaḥ |
children.translated_text: When [the principle] is tranquil, He appears tranquil; when joyful, joyful; when deluded, confused;

children.text: tattvagaṇe sati bhagavān na punaḥ paramārthataḥ sa tathā || 38 ||
children.translated_text: the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) [appears thus] in the presence of the host of principles (<s>tattva</s>), but in ultimate reality He is not so. (38)

children.text: yad anātmany api tadrūpāvabhāsanaṃ tat purā nirākṛtya |
children.translated_text: Having first negated that appearance of His own form even in the not-self,
the supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>) then shatters the delusion of the not-self's form in the Self. (39)
Thus, when the root of both [kinds of] delusion has been completely severed, for one who has attained fulfillment,
no other task whatsoever ever remains for the supreme yogin (<s>parayogin</s>). (40)

children.text: pṛthivī prakṛtir māyā tritayam idaṃ vedyarūpatāpatitam |
children.translated_text: Earth, <s>Prakṛti</s>, and <s>Māyā</s>—this triad, which has fallen into the nature of the knowable,
through the force of the contemplation of non-duality (<s>advaitabhāvanā</s>), becomes indeed a mere residue of pure being (<s>sanmātra</s>). (41)
Just as when one abandons the difference of necklace, bracelet, and bangle, gold alone is seen,
so when difference is abandoned, everything shines as pure being (<s>sanmātra</s>) alone. (42)

children.text: tad brahma paraṃ śuddhaṃ śāntaṃ abhedātmakaṃ samaṃ sakalam |
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahman</s>—supreme, pure, tranquil, of the nature of non-difference, equal, whole,
immortal, true—reposes in <s>Śakti</s>, whose nature is luminosity. (43)

children.text: iṣyata iti vedyata iti saṃpādyata iti ca bhāsvarūpeṇa |
children.translated_text: "It is desired," "it is known," "it is accomplished"—[these are] through its luminous nature;

children.text: aparāmṛṣṭaṃ yad api tu nabhaḥprasūnatvam abhyeti || 44 ||
children.translated_text: yet that which remains untouched [by these predicates] attains the status of a sky-flower [i.e., unreality]. (44)
Through the method of encompassing [all] by the trident of <s>Śaktis</s>, everything [is resolved] in the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśa</s>),
in the ultimate reality bearing the name <s>Śiva</s>, emitted by the God of gods (<s>Devadeva</s>). (45)

children.text: punar api ca pañcaśaktiprasaraṇakrameṇa bahir api tat |
children.translated_text: And again, through the sequential expansion of the five <s>Śaktis</s>, externally too,
the variegated threefold egg (<s>aṇḍatraya</s>) has been created through the attainment of external selfhood. (46)
Thus, driving the mechanism of the wheel of <s>Śaktis</s> through the play [of creation], the God [declares]:
"I alone, of pure nature, am established in the station of the lord of the great wheel of <s>Śaktis</s>." (47)

children.text: mayy eva bhāti viśvaṃ darpaṇa iva nirmale ghatādīni |
children.translated_text: "In me alone the universe shines, like pots and the like in a clear mirror;

children.text: mattaḥ prasarati sarvaṃ svapnavicitratvam iva suptāt || 48 ||
children.translated_text: from me alone everything flows forth, like the variety of a dream from one who sleeps." (48)

children.text: aham eva viśvarūpaḥ karacaranādisvabhāva iva dehaḥ |
children.translated_text: "I alone am of the form of the universe, as the body is of the nature of hands, feet, and the rest;

children.text: sarvasmin aham eva sphurāmi bhāveṣu bhāsvarūpam iva || 49 ||
children.translated_text: in all things I alone flash forth, like luminosity in [all] entities." (49)
"The seer, the hearer, the smeller—though devoid of body and organs, though a non-agent,
I alone compose the wondrous <s>siddhāntas</s> (established doctrines), <s>āgamas</s> (scriptures), and systems of reasoning." (50)

children.text: itthaṃ dvaitavikalpe galite pravilaṅghya mohinīṃ māyām |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the conceptual construction of duality has dissolved, having transcended the deluding <s>Māyā</s>,

children.text: salile salilaṃ kṣīre kṣīram iva brahmaṇi layī syāt || 51 ||
children.translated_text: one should merge into <s>Brahman</s> as water into water, as milk into milk. (51)
Thus, when the host of principles has, through contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), attained the state of being pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: kaḥ śokaḥ ko mohaḥ sarvaṃ brahmāvalokayataḥ || 52 ||
children.translated_text: what grief, what delusion [can there be] for one who beholds everything as <s>Brahman</s>? (52)

children.text: karmaphalaṃ śubham aśubhaṃ mithyājñānena saṃgamād eva |
children.translated_text: The fruit of action (<s>karma</s>), whether auspicious or inauspicious, arises only from association with false knowledge;
for the fault of association is indeed pernicious—just as association with a thief [brings guilt] even upon one who is not a thief. (53)
Those fools who in this world worship the ignorance produced by worldly transactions,
they go to [repeated] birth and death, bound by the bolts of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). (54)
But even <s>karma</s> (action), which is of the nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, accumulated over the time of ignorance—
like cotton long accumulated, [karma] perishes by the power of the radiance of knowledge. // 55 //

children.text: jñānaprāptau kṛtam api na phalāya tato 'sya janma katham |
children.translated_text: When knowledge is attained, even [previously] performed [karma] does not bear fruit; how then could there be a [new] birth for this one?
Freed from the bondage of [past] births, the sun of <s>Śiva</s> shines by its own rays. // 56 //
Just as a seed freed from husk, chaff, and bran produces a sprout,
not so does the <s>ātman</s> (self), liberated from <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>karma</s> [<s>malas</s>], [produce] a sprout of worldly existence. // 57 //

children.text: ātmajño na kutaścana bibheti sarvaṃ hi tasya nijarūpam |
children.translated_text: The knower of the Self fears nothing whatsoever, for everything is his own nature;

children.text: naiva ca śocati yasmāt paramārthe nāśitā nāsti || 58 ||
children.translated_text: nor does he grieve, because in the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>) there is no destruction. // 58 //
From the treasure-heap of supreme truth-gems sprouted in the exceedingly secret treasury of the heart,

children.text: aham eveti maheśvarabhāve kā durgatiḥ kasya || 59 ||
children.translated_text: 'I alone [am all]'—in such a state of being the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>), what misfortune could befall whom? // 59 //

children.text: mokṣasya naiva kiṃcid dhāmāsti na cāpi gamanam anyatra |
children.translated_text: Liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) has no particular abode, nor is there any going elsewhere;
the breaking of the knot of ignorance, the manifestation of one's own power—that is <s>mokṣa</s>. // 60 //
One whose knot of ignorance is broken, whose doubts have departed, whose delusions are dispelled,
whose merit and demerit are exhausted—even while connected with a body, that one is liberated. // 61 //
Just as a seed burned by fire becomes incapable of sprouting,

children.text: jñānāgnidagdham evaṃ karma na janmapradaṃ bhavati || 62 ||
children.translated_text: so too <s>karma</s> burned by the fire of knowledge does not give rise to birth. // 62 //
For, due to limited understanding, through the mental impression (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of a future body appropriate to [past] <s>karma</s>,
consciousness (<s>citi</s>), contracted, upon the destruction of this body, manifests accordingly. // 63 //
But if one [realizes] pure consciousness (<s>bodha</s>), transcending all [duality of] knower and agent,
expansive, of the nature of a light that has neither set nor risen, [having] true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>), // 64 //
free from the division of space and time, permanent, imperishable, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), perfectly full,
the sole agent of the dissolution and arising of the multitude of manifold powers, // 65 //
well-versed in the creative functions beginning with creation—if one realizes the Self as pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: katham iva saṃsārī syād vitatasya kutaḥ kva vā saraṇam || 66 ||
children.translated_text: how could one be a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being)? For one who is all-pervading, whence and where would there be transmigration? // 66 //

children.text: iti yuktibhir api siddhaṃ yatkarma jñānino na saphalaṃ tat |
children.translated_text: Thus, it is established by reasoning too that <s>karma</s> does not bear fruit for the knower;

children.text: na mamedam api tu tasyeti dārḍhyato na hi phalaṃ loke || 67 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is not mine, but His'—from such firmness [of conviction], there is no fruit in this world. // 67 //
Thus, the awakened one, having [offered] all mental constructs (<s>vikalpas</s>) through the wind of contemplation (<s>bhāvanā</s>),
into the blazing fire of the light of the Self, offering [them as] oblations, becomes made of light. // 68 //

children.text: aśnan yad vā tad vā saṃvīto yena kenacic chāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: Eating whatever comes, clothed in whatever is available, at peace,
dwelling wherever—the Self of all beings is liberated. // 69 //
Even if one performs hundreds of thousands of horse sacrifices (<s>aśvamedha</s>), or commits sins amounting to <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin),

children.text: paramārthavin na puṇyair na ca pāpaiḥ spṛśyate vimalaḥ || 70 ||
children.translated_text: the knower of the supreme truth is not touched by merits or demerits—[such a one is] pure. // 70 //
Abandoning intoxication, elation, anger, passion, dejection, fear, greed, and delusion,
free from hymns of praise and ritual exclamations (<s>vaṣaṭkāra</s>), one should wander like an inert person, with a mind beyond dispute. // 71 //
This group [of emotions] beginning with intoxication and elation arises from the delusion of differentiation;
how then can one who has awakened to the non-dual Self be touched by them at all? // 72 //

children.text: stutyaṃ vā hotavyaṃ nāsti vyatiriktam asya kiṃcana ca |
children.translated_text: There is nothing separate from him that could be praised or offered as oblation;

children.text: stotrādinā sa tuṣyen muktas tan nirnamaskṛtivaṣaṭkaḥ || 73 ||
children.translated_text: he who would be pleased by praise and the like is bound—therefore, [the liberated one is] free from obeisance and ritual exclamations. // 73 //
Consisting of the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles), full of the windows of bodily structure,

children.text: nijam anyad atha śarīraṃ ghaṭādi vā tasya devagṛham || 74 ||
children.translated_text: one's own body, or another body, or even a pot and such—[all is] a temple of God for him. // 74 //
And there, the deity [that is] the supreme Self, the great <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, endowed with His own powers—
[the knower] continually worships with the pure offerings of Self-awareness (<s>ātmāmarśana</s>). // 75 //
For one who offers the great seed-collection of the distinction between external and internal, and the absence of mental construction,
into the blazing fire of consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), the <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation) occurs effortlessly, without exertion. // 76 //

children.text: dhyānam anastamitaṃ punar eṣa hi bhagavān vicitrarūpāṇi |
children.translated_text: And <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is unceasing, for this blessed Lord creates manifold forms—
that itself is <s>dhyāna</s>, since the forms depicted by His will are real. // 77 //
The entire series of worlds, the arrangement of the <s>tattva</s>-hierarchy, and the collection of sense organs—

children.text: antarbodhe parivartayati ca yat so 'sya japa uditaḥ || 78 ||
children.translated_text: that which [the Lord] revolves within [His own] awareness—that is declared to be His <s>japa</s> (recitation). // 78 //

children.text: sarvaṃ samayā dṛṣṭyā yat paśyati yac ca saṃvidaṃ manute |
children.translated_text: All that he sees with an equal vision, and whatever consciousness he contemplates,
[seeing her as] delighting in the universal cremation-ground, adorned with the <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) fashioned from the body, // 79 //
the skull-cup formed from the fragment of the knowable (<s>vedya</s>), held in his own hand, filled with the wine of universal <s>rasa</s> (essence)—

children.text: rasayati ca yat tad etad vratam asya sudurlabhaṃ ca sulabhaṃ ca || 80 ||
children.translated_text: that which he savors—this is his <s>vrata</s> (sacred observance), both supremely difficult and supremely easy. // 80 //
Thus, having realized the supreme truth named <s>Maheśvara</s>, free from birth and death,
through the shining forth of the knower-nature, one who has accomplished what was to be accomplished remains as one pleases. // 81 //
The all-pervading [Self], thus described as the Self of all, with all multiplicity shaken off,

children.text: nirupamaparamānandaṃ yo vetti sa tanmayo bhavati || 82 ||
children.translated_text: of incomparable supreme bliss—whoever knows this becomes identical with That. // 82 //

children.text: tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham |
children.translated_text: Whether at a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred place) or in the house of a <s>śvapaca</s> (outcaste), even having lost memory, abandoning the body—
one liberated simultaneously with knowledge attains <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom), with sorrow destroyed. // 83 //
Service at sacred places leads to merit; death in an outcaste's dwelling leads to hell—
but when there is no contact with the stain of merit or demerit, what [difference does] that [make]? // 84 //
The placing of pieces of husk among rice grains that have been well-separated from husk and chaff
does not again produce identity in nature [of those rice grains] with that [husk]. // 85 //
Likewise, consciousness (<s>saṃvid</s>), separated from the covering of sheaths (<s>kañcuka</s>), here, due to [residual] impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
even though remaining [in the body], the liberated self is free from contact with them. // 86 //
The purification fashioned by the most skillful artisan [remains even] when separated from the container;
a gem, though dirty from its setting, when the setting is removed, is in its true nature transparent. // 87 //
Thus, knowledge (<s>vedana</s>) that has attained a pure state through the teaching of a true <s>guru</s>, [though housed in] the body as a container,
even when liberated, appears as if devoid of another container—[shining in] the nature of <s>Śiva</s>. // 88 //
Through the authority of scripture and the like, with unwavering faith, having attained identity with That,

children.text: prāptaḥ sa eva pūrvaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ manuṣyatvam || 89 ||
children.translated_text: that very one [who] previously [experienced] heaven, hell, or human state— // 89 //

children.text: antyaḥ kṣaṇas tu tasmin puṇyāṃ pāpāṃ ca vā sthitiṃ puṣyan |
children.translated_text: but the last moment, strengthening either a meritorious or sinful state in him,

children.text: mūḍhānāṃ sahakārībhāvaṃ gacchati gatau tu na sa hetuḥ || 90 ||
children.translated_text: plays merely a cooperative role for the deluded; it is not, however, the cause of the [final] destination. // 90 //
Even those who know their own destination as identical with That—animals, birds, reptiles, and the like—
they too, refined by the impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) of ancient awakening, attain that destination. // 91 //

children.text: svargamayo nirayamayas tad ayaṃ dehāntarālagaḥ puruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) existing within the body is either of a heavenly or hellish nature;
upon the destruction of that [body], by its own propensity, it takes on another body. // 92 //

children.text: evaṃ jñānāvasare svātmā sakṛd asya yādṛg avabhātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, at the moment of knowledge, whatever form one's own Self has once appeared as,

children.text: tādṛśa eva tadāsau na dehapāte 'nyathā bhavati || 93 ||
children.translated_text: exactly that is its nature then—it does not become otherwise at the fall of the body. // 93 //
The withdrawal of the sense-faculties, destruction of memory, labored breathing, cessation [of breath],
specific pains in the vital points (<s>marmas</s>)—this is the experience born of bodily dispositions. // 94 //

children.text: sa kathaṃ vigrahayoge sati na bhavet tena mohayoge 'pi |
children.translated_text: How could that [experience] not occur while connected with a body? Yet, even in that state of delusion,
at the moment of death, the knower does not deviate from the supreme truth of one's own Self. // 95 //

children.text: paramārthamārgam enaṃ jhaṭiti yadā gurumukhāt samabhyeti |
children.translated_text: When one suddenly enters this path of supreme truth from the mouth of the <s>guru</s>,
through an exceedingly intense descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>), one becomes <s>Śiva</s> at that very moment, without any obstacle. // 96 //
For one who gradually ascends to the form that transcends all, step by step,
upon attaining establishment in the highest <s>tattva</s> (reality), at the end, [there is] becoming one with <s>Śiva</s>. // 97 //

children.text: tasya tu paramārthamayīṃ dhārām agatasya madhyaviśrānteḥ |
children.translated_text: But for one who has not attained the stream of supreme truth, who rests at an intermediate stage,
even though his mind is eager to attain that state—death may sometimes occur. // 98 //
He is called in scripture a <s>yogabhraṣṭa</s> (one fallen from yoga); [he becomes] lord of a realm of varied enjoyments;
according to the stage at which he rested, having [experienced that], in another birth he becomes <s>Śiva</s>. // 99 //

children.text: paramārthamārgam enaṃ hy abhyasyāprāpya yogam api nāma |
children.translated_text: Indeed, one who practices this path of supreme truth, even without actually attaining <s>yoga</s>,
becomes a partaker of the pleasures of the divine world, rejoicing with a delighted mind for a long time. // 100 //

children.text: viṣayeṣu sārvabhaumaḥ sarvajanaiḥ pūjyate yathā rājā |
children.translated_text: Just as a king, sovereign over all objects of enjoyment, is honored by all people,
so is the <s>yogabhraṣṭa</s> honored by all the gods in the [celestial] realms. // 101 //

children.text: mahatā kālena punar mānuṣyaṃ prāpya yogam abhyasya |
children.translated_text: After a great length of time, having again attained human birth and practiced <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: prāpnoti divyam amṛtam yasmād āvartate na punaḥ || 102 ||
children.translated_text: one attains the divine nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) from which there is no return. // 102 //

children.text: tasmāt sanmārge 'smin nirato yaḥ kaścid eti sa śivatvam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, whoever is devoted to this true path attains <s>Śivatva</s> (the state of <s>Śiva</s>);

children.text: iti matvā paramārthe yathā tathāpi prayatanīyam || 103 ||
children.translated_text: knowing this, one should strive in the supreme truth by whatever means possible. // 103 //
This compendium, composed by <s>Abhinavagupta</s>—for one who meditates upon the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,
the state of <s>Śiva</s> quickly enters one's own heart. // 104 //

children.text: āryāśatena tad idaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ śāstrasāram atigūḍham |
children.translated_text: This essence of the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture), exceedingly profound, has been summarized in one hundred <s>āryā</s> verses,
by me, <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, illumined by the remembrance of the feet of <s>Śiva</s>. // 105 //
